fix.notes: The `playability.rank()` call loads all card ranks (one DB query over the precomputed `_playability` table) on each uncached card page load. The `card()` endpoint is decorated `@cached()`, so this is only a concern on cache misses. The stats.mustache partial is also used in person.mustache; no rank is set for persons, so the conditional blocks simply don't render there.
fix.pr_body: ## What was missing The card detail page (`/cards//`) showed win record, tournament results, and Elo, but did not show the card's overall playability **rank** — a pre-computed metric already available via `playability.rank()` that tells you how a card ranks among all Penny Dreadful legal cards by playability score. ## What changed - **`decksite/controllers/metagame.py`**: In the `card()` controller, added `from decksite.data import playability` and one line `c.rank = playability.rank().get(c.name)` after loading the card — sets the rank on the card object before the view is rendered. - **`decksite/templates/stats.mustache`**: Added a conditional `{{#rank}}Rank{{/rank}}` header and `{{#rank}}#{{rank}}{{/rank}}` data cell, matching the existing pattern used for the Elo column. The rank is only shown when the card has a positive playability rank; cards with zero playability (or that appear in the `person.mustache` context where rank is not set) render no column. ## Validation - `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed (ruff auto-fixed import ordering on the new `playability` import). - `uv run --frozen python dev.py unit` — 845 passed, 1 skipped in 18.87s. Fixes #12105

evidence.detail: rank() returns dict[str, int] of card name to rank, derived from _playability table via ROW_NUMBER().
ranks_select() SQL assigns NULL rank to cards with zero playability, otherwise ranks by playability DESC.
rank is already exposed in the /api/cards JSON feed but not in the card detail view.
Card detail template renders stats.mustache for played cards and lists decks, but has no rank display.
load_card() does not include rank in its SQL or assign it to the returned card object.

Total change ~10 lines across 2 files.
triage.notes: rank() returns overall all-time rank (not per-season), which is appropriate for a card detail page. The card view's __getattr__ delegates to self.card so setting c.rank on the Container makes it accessible in the template without changing views/card.py.
